distinguishing_features: Passive mass-loading to detune a subsea pipeline span's natural frequency away from the vortex-shedding frequency
Discrete high-density blocks placed at span interior points rather than adding damping, stiffening, or changing wall thickness
Kill condition based on existing pressure-fluctuation monitoring at the shedding frequency
No new sensors, no operational intervention, and no hydraulic modification
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce vortex-induced vibration fatigue of an existing subsea pipeline span without adding monitoring hardware or changing the pipe structure
parsed.viable_reason: Adding sufficient discrete mass to lower the first-mode natural frequency below the Strouhal shedding frequency is physically feasible and can suppress lock-in without violating the no-new-monitoring constraint.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the supplied prior art concerns subsea VIV, mass-tuning, or pressure-fluctuation-based VIV detection, so the specific mass-block detuning mechanism and its pressure-based falsification test are not obvious extensions of that art.
